question.text: Mr. Rajiv Kapoor, Head of Product at Lotus Capital AIF, is drafting a new Private Equity scheme under Category II. He proposes an open-ended structure to allow quarterly redemptions. As compliance officer, how do you respond?

answer.text: Permissible with SEBI approval and a redemption gate
Permissible only if 75% of unit-holders consent up-front
Not permissible — Category I and II AIFs MUST be close-ended with a minimum tenure of 3 years
Permissible if the fund limits redemptions to Accredited Investors only

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Regulation 13 of SEBI (AIF) Regulations requires that Category I and Category II AIFs be compulsorily close-ended with a minimum tenure of 3 years (computed from date of first close). This is because underlying PE/VC/Debt/Infra investments are illiquid and cannot service recurring redemptions. Only Category III AIFs may be open-ended. **The Trap:** Options A/B/D invent conditional pathways that do not exist. The '75% unit-holder consent' route is the one used for associate transactions (Reg 15), not for changing the fundamental open/close structure. AI-only schemes still must be close-ended for Cat I/II. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C/XIX-A also test the close-ended mandate. XIX-E (Cat III — future) would permit open-ended since hedge funds need daily subscription/redemption. XXI-B PMS runs on separately managed accounts, not close/open-ended pooling. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** When designing a PE fund, the close-ended mandate is actually a feature for LPs — it prevents 'run-on-the-fund' risk during vintage cycle downturns and lets the Manager hold illiquid investments to optimal exit. Structure the commitment period (3-4 yrs), investment period and harvest period distinctly in the PPM.
